chyp-rs
Copyright 2026 the chyp-rs contributors

This product is an unofficial Rust port of part of Chyp, "an interactive
theorem prover for string diagrams":

  Chyp
  Copyright (C) 2022-2023 Aleks Kissinger
  https://github.com/akissinger/chyp
  Ported from commit 3d28483 ("fixed some bugs in the docs").
  Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.

It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Aleks Kissinger or the Chyp project.

The files under src/ whose header contains "Derived from Chyp" (checker.rs,
graph.rs, layout.rs, matcher.rs, parser.rs, parts.rs, proofstate.rs,
rewrite.rs, rule.rs, state.rs) are modified translations of the Chyp source
files named in that header, which also reproduces their copyright notices
and lists what was changed. The other files are new.

Test fixtures and law files:
  - tests/fixtures/upstream/ holds Chyp's examples/frobenius.chyp, hopf.chyp,
    module.chyp and smc.chyp, copied unmodified from commit 3d28483.
  - tests/fixtures/derived/proof_test_explicit.chyp is derived from Chyp's
    examples/proof_test.chyp, and tests/fixtures/derived/ssfa_inlined.chyp
    from examples/frobenius.chyp and examples/ssfa.chyp; the changes are
    listed at the top of each file.
  - laws/sync_spiders.chyp adapts the Frobenius-algebra rules and the frobL
    and frobR proofs of Chyp's examples/frobenius.chyp, as stated at its top.
  - tests/fixtures/original/ and tests/fixtures/crash/ are original to
    chyp-rs, as are laws/orderers.chyp, filters.chyp and drivers.chyp.
  - tests/fixtures/pflow/ holds the theories of pflow.xyz's Laws view, copied
    unmodified; sync-spiders.chyp there contains the frobL and frobR proofs
    and the Frobenius axioms' presentation from Chyp's examples/frobenius.chyp.
  - tests/fixtures/expected/ holds the results of running upstream Chyp
    (commit 3d28483) on those files, produced by tools/upstream_expected.py.

Chyp is by Aleks Kissinger and the Chyp contributors; Alexander Koziell-Pipe
wrote much of its graph and matching code (chyp/graph.py, chyp/matcher.py).
The theory it implements is from the "String Diagram Rewrite Theory" papers
I-III by Bonchi, Gadducci, Kissinger, Sobocinski and Zanasi
(arXiv:2012.01847, arXiv:2104.14686, arXiv:2109.06049).
